title: One day, one tribute game: how Claude, an image model, ElevenLabs and Suno made a browser beat 'em up)
author: Brennor20101987
selftext:
A viral video from Nice: a game shop clerk standing in his doorway to protect his shop. We turned it into a free browser game in one day. How the work split:



\- Claude: all the code, Phaser 3 in plain JavaScript, no bundler. 12 waves, 11 moves, 8 passives, 3 bosses, 3 ults, EN/FR/RU, an Android build. A test bot plays the whole game headless to check the balance.

\- An image model: the pixel-art sprites, the street, the anime cut-ins. It kept drawing real characters (an anime fighter, a yellow chomper with a ghost) whenever a prompt said "game hero", so every prompt now says "original characters only, no logos".

\- Animation: the image model gives one good pose, not a consistent walk cycle. So Claude wrote a tool that cuts each character into a paper doll (body, arms, thighs, shins, shoes) and walks it with 2-bone IK, feet planted (picture below).

\- ElevenLabs: 53 sound effects and 17 French voice lines for the hero. New lines are generated in several takes, and Whisper picks the one it understands best.

\- Suno: the music (I made the tracks).



The lesson: the slowest part wasn't code, it was balance. The first version was so easy that even the clumsy test bot won.



Play free in the browser or on Android: [https://brennor123.itch.io/le-final-boss](https://brennor123.itch.io/le-final-boss)
